summary: Transit Gateway route-propagation lag leads to VPCE region-mismatch and presigned model artifact 403s for Private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer reported repeated 403 when the Private deployment agent attempts to download model artifacts from S3 using presigned URLs. Error only observed for workloads in us-west-2 after a Transit Gateway maintenance window.
impact: Multiple model-serving pods failed to warm caches for NimbleHealth private cluster in us-west-2 resulting in degraded latency and request failures for production traffic. Estimated 30% of model pulls returned 403 during the window.
environment_details: Private deployment (VPC-connected control plane). Transit Gateway used for peering between customer VPC and provider VPC where VPCE (interface endpoint) lives. VPCE returns 403 for presigned GETs when routed to eu-west-1 endpoint by mistake.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a private agent in a VPC attached to the TGW with route propagation enabled
2) Request model artifact URL from control plane for openlm/7b-v2
3) Attempt curl -v to the presigned S3 URL from a node in us-west-2 during TGW route convergence
4) Observe HTTP 403 when traffic egress is routed to the wrong AZ/region VPCE back-end
5) Remove the erroneous route from the propagation table and retry; downloads succeed
logs: 2025-11-03T04:12:23Z control-plane INFO issued_presigned_url region=us-west-2 bucket=nimble-models key=openlm-7b-v2/model.tar.gz
2025-11-03T04:12:24Z vpc-flow log src=10.0.24.18 dst=vpce-0a1b2c3d4e.local dst_region=eu-west-1 proto=TCP action=ACCEPT
2025-11-03T04:12:24Z tcpdump: TLS SNI: s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com but TCP egress went to 10.50.2.200 (vpce-eni eu-west-1)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: presigned URL signature mismatch — rejected. URL signature valid and created for us-west-2.
Verified presigned URL in control plane and reproduced 403 from a node in customer's VPC.
VPC Flow Logs and tcpdump show outbound TCP to a VPCE ENI that is in eu-west-1, not us-west-2.
Transit Gateway route table had a stale propagated route pointing to an older attachment (attachment-12345) in a peered AZ which resolved via a different region's VPCE.
AWS TGW maintenance during a background NVA failover delayed route replacement propagation leading to asymmetry for ~7 minutes.
When traffic reached the eu-west-1 VPCE backend, S3 verified region in the host header against the presigned-signed region and returned 403 (signature/region mismatch).
root_cause: Transit Gateway route propagation lag after maintenance caused egress traffic from nodes in us-west-2 to be sent to a VPCE endpoint in eu-west-1. The presigned URL was region-scoped; S3 rejected requests arriving at a different region endpoint with HTTP 403.
workaround_resolution: Immediate mitigation: removed stale propagated route from TGW route table and added a temporary static route forcing egress via the correct attachment. Control plane also issued a retry/backoff for artifact pulls which allowed warm-up to resume.
permanent_fix: AWS operations confirmed propagation delay during failover is a known edge case. Recommended changes applied: (1) update Private deployment TGW route monitoring to detect mismatched VPCE ENI regions and alert; (2) add conservative retry/backoff with 30s jitter and a region-validate check before finalizing presigned URLs; (3) runbook updated to include an automated static route insertion during detected TGW propagation anomalies.
resolution_notes: Resolved on 2025-11-07 after TGW propagation stabilized and static route removed. Customer confirmed model pulls successful and production latency returned to baseline. Follow-up runbook, monitoring alert, and PR #1286 merged to add region validation and retry logic.
follow_up_actions: 1) Ops: Create CloudWatch metric for TGW propagation latency and set P1 alert (owner: infra-ops)
2) Dev: Merge PR #1286 to add region check to artifact download flow and increased retry with jitter (owner: platform-engineering)
3) CS: Notify NimbleHealth of root cause and provide postmortem link (owner: customer-success)
4) Runbook: Add TGW rollback checklist and automated static-route playbook (owner: network-eng)
5) Schedule DR test to simulate TGW attachment failover and validate route convergence (owner: reliability)
